about.title: Fowler Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Fowler is small enough that one loss is felt across town. Public records for 2025 list 28 injury collisions inside the city, 39 people hurt, and one traffic death — a count that stays abstract until the name on the report is your spouse, parent, or child. Crash reports here cluster along Golden State Boulevard, SR-99 and its northbound lanes, and Manning Avenue, with a Thursday-morning peak between 7 and 9 a.m. A wrongful death claim under California law is a civil action, entirely separate from anything the CHP or a prosecutor chooses to pursue. It allows the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children — and in certain situations other dependents or heirs — to seek compensation for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Fowler families with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Fowler Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing to the spouse or domestic partner and children first, then to certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who in your family qualifies before anyone signs anything.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims against a city, county, or state agency carry a much shorter clock. Early legal review protects that window.

items.title: A civil path that does not wait on the criminal case
items.desc: Whether or not charges are filed, your family can pursue funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance through a separate civil action. There is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on SR-99 near Fowler. Does it matter that the highway is state-maintained?
items.answer: It can. If part of the claim involves a public entity — for example, a roadway condition maintained by the state — California requires a government claim within a far shorter period than the standard two years. That is one reason families in Fowler are encouraged to speak with an attorney soon after a fatal collision on SR-99, Golden State Boulevard, or Manning Avenue rather than waiting for the investigation to close.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there are none, certain other heirs or people who were financially dependent on the deceased may have standing. Because these rules are specific, an attorney will usually confirm eligibility before moving forward.

items.question: Do we have to wait for the criminal case to finish before filing a civil claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death lawsuit is a separate civil matter, and it can proceed regardless of whether a prosecutor files charges or how any criminal case ends. Waiting can actually hurt, because the two-year civil deadline keeps running during a criminal proceeding.
